prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1487; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my name on tape, but you can note that I'm the driver of the vehicle involved.
Q: That's fine, we'll note you as the driver. Can you describe where the collision happened?
A: It was on a two-lane road in Baytown, Texas, near a shopping center entrance. Traffic was slow that afternoon.
Q: What speed were you traveling when the other vehicle came into your lane?
A: I'd guess I was going maybe fifteen miles an hour. I had just started to slow down for a turn.
Q: Did you apply your brakes before impact?
A: Yes, I braked as soon as I saw the other car drifting toward me. We still hit nearly head-on, but it wasn't a hard hit.
Q: Did your airbags deploy?
A: No, they didn't. I was able to get out of the car on my own.
Q: Did you seek medical attention after the collision?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic the same day. They checked my neck and lower back and said I had strains.
Q: Describe your symptoms as they stand now.
A: My neck is stiff, especially when I turn my head to check mirrors. My lower back aches after sitting for more than twenty minutes. Some mornings it's worse.
Q: Have you missed any work or daily activities because of these symptoms?
A: I've had to leave early a couple of times, and I've skipped my usual weekend yard work.
Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I've been cooperating fully and I'm working with my own doctor on physical therapy. I'll send the paperwork when I have it.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
A: Thank you.
